name: Required Reason: system boot time
meaning: Boot timestamp is a stable fingerprint until reboot. 35F9.1 measures in-app intervals, 8FFB.1 stamps in-app events, 3D61.1 adds it to a user-submitted bug report.

android.api_surface: Android has no gate: elapsedRealtime is open

ios.revocation: App Review: no off-device boot time
ios.api_surface: 35F9.1 measure elapsed time in-app; 8FFB.1 absolute timestamps for in-app events; 3D61.1 optional bug report, shown to user

limits.headline: Can check how long the phone has been on; iPhone needs an approved reason
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the app measures time or logs an event
can: Measure time between actions inside the app (reason 35F9.1)
Add it to a bug report that you send (reason 3D61.1)
Check uptime with no gate on Android
cannot: Check it on iPhone without one of the three approved reasons
Be used as a fingerprint on iPhone; it stays steady until a restart
Use it on iPhone for ads or tracking
limits.differs: iPhone requires one of three approved reasons; Android has no gate.

story.what_it_is: An iOS rule: apps must give a reason before reading how long the phone has been on.

marketing.name: Required reason APIs
marketing.pitch: Apple requires apps to declare why they use certain system timers and data in their privacy manifest.

story.for_you: You never see it. Apps that read the phone's boot time must tell Apple why. This makes it harder for them to use a hidden number that stays the same until a restart.
story.for_makers: The boot time can stitch together separate apps and sessions. Apple now limits its use to timers, in app event stamps and a bug report. Makers must describe their use in a privacy manifest or risk store rejection.

use_cases.example: A game measures how long a level takes using the boot clock as a stopwatch.
A video app times buffering and playback using uptime.
An analytics SDK stamps events with uptime and must declare it.
An ad SDK could use boot time as part of a hidden device fingerprint, which is now restricted.
A fraud tool compares boot times to spot emulator farms.
A developer adds the right reason code to the privacy manifest before shipping.
A run tracker times intervals with the system clock.

story.android_note: Android has no gate for reading uptime, so no reason is needed.
story.ios_note: iOS 17 added the rule with three allowed reasons, for in app intervals, in app event stamps and a user submitted bug report.

technical_bounds: Boot time itself may not leave the device (except 3D61.1 reports)
